builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Modulating Merging Strengths via Joint Loss Estimation for LoRA-based Continual Learning
summary: M2LE replaces single scalar-coefficient LoRA merging after each continual-learning task with an element-wise modulation of the LoRA update derived from a Hessian-guided joint loss over previous and current tasks, plus a perturbation-based task-interference simulation during training. The cost is additional computation: Hessian (or Hessian-vector-product) estimation and an analytic solve per task, plus extra perturbation training steps, all feasible on a single 24 GB GPU but adding complexity to the fine-tuning loop. What can fail is Hessian approximation quality on small compute budgets, sensitivity of the analytic solution to noisy second-order estimates, and the fact that the method only applies if the reader's workload is sequential multi-task fine-tuning with LoRA adapters.
rationale: The method targets continual LoRA fine-tuning, which fits constrained infrastructure, but the quality gain is unquantified in the abstract and depends on Hessian estimation stability, so it warrants a workload-specific pilot before production adoption.
technique: Element-wise LoRA merge modulation for continual learning

The cost is additional computation: Hessian (or Hessian-vector-product) estimation and an analytic solve per task, plus extra perturbation training steps, all feasible on a single 24 GB GPU but adding complexity to the fine-tuning loop. What can fail is Hessian approximation quality on small compute budgets, sensitivity of the analytic solution to noisy second-order estimates, and the fact that the method only applies if the reader's workload is sequential multi-task fine-tuning with LoRA adapters.
The abstract states M2LE consistently outperforms existing PEFT-based continual learning methods on multiple benchmarks, with no specific numeric margin given.
